### Browser tools on chat sessions

> [
!NOTE]\n>\n> Hosted browser availability depends on the account and deployment. The browser workspace must be enabled to open the
live pane in the Playground.\n\n`POST /chat-sessions/messages` accepts an optional `browser: { policy?, profileId? }`. Attach it o
n every turn that should browse. The initial grant and profile are fixed; the current host policy and pinned read-only mode can na
rrow the effective permissions. Responses and traces include the read-only `chatSessionId`, browser metadata, and screenshot URLs

without inline image data.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| - | - | - |
| POST | `/chat-sessions/browser` | Create an empty API
session and its browser with `projectId`, `policy`, optional `profileId`, and a stable `idempotencyKey`. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessio
ns/{sessionId}/browser/open` | Open or wake the session browser. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/command` | Execut
e a browser command under the session policy with a stable `commandId`. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/note` | Ap
pend a command-ledger note. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/trace` | Read command receipts and screenshot evidence
. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/artifact` | Resolve a command screenshot URL. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessi
onId}/browser/close` | Release the session desktop. |\n\nOnly the owning user can drive an API session's browser. All inputs use t
he public `sessionId`; conversation and browser identifiers in responses are informational. Capacity refusals before execution rel
ease the turn lease so the same idempotency key can be retried. An execution with an unknown outcome must be inspected before atte

mpting a new action.

# Local Evals

> Run an MCPJam eval suite file on your machine with m

cpjam test with local results and an MCPJam identity

> [!NOTE]
>
> The upcoming SDK 10, CLI 6, and Vitest 0.3 releases requir
e an MCPJam login or `sk_` API key for every eval, including BYOK runs with uploads disabled. These versions must ship after the b
ackend run-start endpoint is deployed. Earlier versions keep their existing behavior.\n\n`mcpjam test <file>` runs an MCPJam suite
file locally: it connects your MCP servers, drives each case's prompts through a model, grades the transcript with the same asser
tions a hosted run uses, and decides the run with the same verdict policy. Bring your own provider key and authenticate the run wi
th MCPJam. With MCPJam-hosted inference it uses your existing CLI login and billing.\n\nResults are **never uploaded**. The comman
d writes results to your terminal and, if you ask, to a report file. It records the run start with MCPJam. Like every command, it
sends the CLI's single anonymous [telemetry](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/telemetry.md) event, which `--no-telemetry` or `DO_NOT_TR

ACK=1` turns off; the run adds no telemetry of its own.

## Eval identity and local data

Run `mcpjam cloud login` locally, or
set `MCPJAM_API_KEY` to an organization `sk_` key in CI. The SDK also accepts `apiKey` or `mcpjamAuth` in run options. Explicit c
redentials take precedence over `MCPJAM_API_KEY`, which takes precedence over the saved CLI login. An invalid explicit credential
never falls back to another account. CI never starts an interactive login. Ask an organization admin for a key if you cannot creat
e one.\n\nEvery logical run needs an online start response. MCPJam retries transient failures within ten seconds, then stops befor
e execution. A prior successful run does not enable offline execution. The CLI resolves the project using its existing `--project`
, environment, and linked-project settings; a key can only access its own organization.\n\nWith results uploads disabled, the star
t-run request sends only the credential in the authorization header, any MCPJam API headers you configure through the SDK's `infer
ence.resolveMcpjam`, project selection, a new run-start ID, client version and surface (SDK, CLI, or Vitest), planned iteration co
unt, provider names, and whether a client profile is used (`unknown` for custom executors). The server resolves the organization a
nd account. The start-run request sends no prompts, outputs, tool calls, or server URLs. MCPJam-hosted inference still sends promp
ts through MCPJam to the model, as before. Retries reuse the same ID. Planned iterations are intent, not completed usage or a char
ge. This release adds no debit, quota draw, or balance refusal.\n\n`DO_NOT_TRACK`, `MCPJAM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED`, and CLI telemetry
settings disable analytics, not the required run-start request. Results remain local unless result uploading is enabled separately

.

## Quick start

### 1. Write a suite

Save this as `.mcpjam/evals/example.yaml`:

```yaml theme={"theme":"css-variab

les"}
schemaVersion: "2"
mode: agentWorkflow
reportingMode: standard
suite:
 id: s_notes_example
 name: Notes server
t

arget:
 servers:
 - name: notes
defaults:
 judge:
 enabled: false
 model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5
 iterations:

1
 passThreshold: 1
 validity: {}
cases:
 - id: c_reads_a_note
 title: reads the note it was asked about
 steps:

- id: s1
 kind: prompt
 prompt: What does note 7 say?
 - id: a1
 kind: assert
 asserti

on:
 type: toolCalledAtLeastOnce
 toolName: read_note
 - id: c_never_deletes
 title: never deletes when

only asked to read
 steps:
 - id: s1
 kind: prompt
 prompt: Summarize note 7.
 - id: a1
 k

ind: assert
 assertion:
 type: toolNeverCalled
 toolName: delete_note
```

`mcpjam cloud eval valid

ate --file .mcpjam/evals/example.yaml` checks the file offline, with no account.

### 2. Configure the server

`mcpjam test` b
inds each `target.servers[].name` to a local MCP config. The simplest is a `.mcp.json` next to where you run the command:\n\n```js

d run

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=[REDACTED]
mcpjam test .mcpjam/evals/example.yaml\

n```
